Do you desire to earn from digital products? You can start small, learn as you go, and build one helpful product at a time. 7 steps to get started 1. Choose a person you want to help.     Think about a group you understand—busy parents, new business owners, job seekers, or beginners learning a skill. 1. Find one problem they need solved.     Ask what they struggle with, search comments and questions online, and listen to the words they use. 1. Pick a simple digital product.     Start with something manageable: a checklist, planner, guide, template, short ebook, or mini-workshop. 1. Create a useful first version.     Make it clear, practical, and easy to use. You can use tools like Canva to design it, but the value comes from helping solve the problem. 1. Set a beginner-friendly price.     For a short guide or checklist, you might test $7–$17. For a more detailed workbook or template bundle, consider $17–$37. Check what similar products offer, then choose a price that fits your product and audience. 1. Choose a place to sell it.     Use a digital-product platform that lets customers pay and receive the file. Read its fees and terms before choosing. 1. Share helpful content and invite people to learn more.     Answer questions, show what your product helps with, and include a clear call to action. Keep improving based on feedback. You don’t need a huge audience to begin, but you do need a product that genuinely helps and a consistent way to reach people.
